observations: Sample-size effect on ranking agreement is REAL and MONOTONIC: canonical recipe tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP agreement goes from 0% at n=5 to 0% at n=10 to 50% at n=15 to 56% at n=20. Spearman correlation = 1.0 (perfect monotonic). C5 PASSES.

BUT the improvement plateaus well below the 80% threshold: agreement at n=20 is only 55.95%, confirming the ranking instability is PARTIALLY sample-size-dependent but NOT fully resolved at the maximum available sample size. C6 FAILS.

Per-task recipe (independent p=0.5 per task) shows BETTER ranking agreement than canonical recipe (shared subset p=0.5) at n=20: 78.65% vs 55.95%. This is the opposite of the eta2 pattern (canonical 0.92 vs per-task 0.37), suggesting that independent per-task sampling captures diverse discriminative elements better for ranking even though it degrades overall eta2.

Non-recipe pipeline ranking agreement: at n=5 and n=10, tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP ranking agreement is FALSE (pipeline reverses listing vs detail). This is because at small subsamples, the non-recipe pipeline's density for tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP produces detail > listing instead of listing > detail. At n=15 and n=20, ranking agreement is TRUE. The non-recipe pipeline DOES require sufficient elements to preserve ranking.

Non-recipe pipeline eta2 for tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP: 0.983 at n=5 (degraded from 0.996 at n=20), suggesting that even without recipe sampling, element subsampling degrades discrimination. The eta2 reduction at small n is from fewer elements contributing to the density sum.

Bootstrap ranking agreement at n=20: 57.1% ± 49.5% (571/1000 bootstrap samples agree). This high variance confirms the ranking is unstable — it depends heavily on which tasks happen to be sampled. The bootstrap CI spans from ~0% to ~100%, indicating the ranking is not reliably preserved at any effective_n in this sample.

The hierarchy density null control reproduces identically (eta2=0.0, all means 3.69e-07), confirming the y-proxy underflow degeneracy from the parent experiment. This is a known limitation, not a new finding.

Within-type template invariance persists: all tasks of the same page type have identical tag_entropy, form_fraction, and total_area values within the truncated-first-20 sample. This means any subsample preserves within-type identity — the ranking test is the only discriminating measure.
validity_notes: The 7 tasks (3 listing, 3 detail, 1 cart deduplicated to n=1) with truncated-first-20 locatable_sample are the input. Full DOM testing (n=21-82) was NOT performed because raw data contains only truncated-first-20 elements. The n=20 result is the maximum achievable from this dataset.

Within-type template invariance: tasks of the same page type share identical element tags/roles/inForm/w/h in the truncated-first-20 sample. Any between-type discriminative mapping trivially yields eta2 close to 1.0 in the non-recipe pipeline. The test is ranking preservation, not magnitude.
Cart n=1 degeneracy: cart page_type has n=1 (deduplicated), making within-type variance degenerate. Comparison focuses on listing vs detail (n=3 each).

Effective_n subsampling uses the first n elements from each task's locatable_sample (ordered by DOM position), not random subsampling. This preserves the DOM-sequential structure but may not represent random element subsets. The monotonic improvement (Spearman=1.0) suggests the first-n approach captures meaningful structure.

Recipe sampling uses 10 seeds × 1000 iterations per effective_n per definition per recipe type. Total computational cost: ~480,000 recipe iterations, ~4000 bootstrap iterations. All offline computation, no browser/network/model calls.

The Spearman correlation is computed on only 4 points (n ∈ {5,10,15,20}). While the correlation is 1.0 (perfect monotonic), the small sample size limits statistical power. The 10-percentage-point improvement criterion provides additional guard against spurious monotonicity.

Per-task recipe seeding uses task_id hash as additional entropy to ensure independent role sampling per task. This differs from the parent experiment's protocol where all tasks shared the same random sequence; the independent approach better represents true per-task recipe behavior.
Single Magento site, single truncated-first-20 sample. Cross-site generalization not tested. Claim ceiling bounded accordingly.
unresolved: Full DOM testing (n=21-82) is still needed for definitive answer on whether ranking stabilizes beyond the truncated-first-20 ceiling. The n=20 result strongly suggests structural instability but does not rule out stabilization at n>20.

The per-task recipe achieves 78.65% ranking agreement at n=20 — tantalizingly close to 80% but not tested by frozen C6 which only requires canonical recipe. A dedicated experiment on per-task recipe ranking stability at full DOM would be informative.

Why does non-recipe pipeline ranking fail at n=5 and n=10 but succeed at n=15 and n=20? The first-5 and first-10 elements may not contain enough discriminative signal. Understanding this threshold could inform element selection strategies.
Cross-site generalization of the sample-size effect remains untested. Different sites may have different template invariance properties, affecting the ranking stability boundary.

The bootstrap CI for ranking agreement at n=20 (57% ± 50%) is extremely wide, suggesting the ranking is not a stable property of this sample. A larger task set (more than 3 per type) would narrow the CI and provide more reliable agreement estimates.
